newsitem.title: FRANCE: Yeltsin tells Clinton Russia won't target NATO.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin tells Clinton Russia won't target NATO.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin told U.S. President Bill Clinton on Tuesday he would extend an agreement not to aim nuclear missiles at U.S. cities to all NATO territory and offered to discuss further confidence-building measures, a U.S. official said.

National Security Adviser Sandy Berger, briefing reporters on an hour-long meeting between the two leaders after the signing of a NATO-Russia agreement in Paris, welcomed Yeltsin's offer as unexpected and "significant".
"I think it's a reflection of the momentum of today, in which Russia and NATO entered a new era of partnership," Berger said. "It is a step which further reduces tensions."

Asked if the United States had been informed in advance of Yeltsin's pledge, he replied: "No, there was no prior indication that President Yeltsin would make that announcement, but it was a welcome one."
Berger said Yeltsin had not elaborated on what further confidence measures he had in mind, but said they should be discussed at expert level.

He said the United States was not taken aback by Yeltsin's impromptu diplomacy. "I think the more significant fact here is that a step was taken in the direction of reducing nuclear tensions and I think that's important and significant," he said.
